A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRAFT and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite pagination and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative reconstructions, and a 53-participant user study in Sections 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds loss ablations and quantitative initialization-robustness results.

M1.justification: The proposed initialization pipeline, 24-token transformer, recurrent refinement, scale update, and default training losses remain unchanged. Additional loss and tokenization variants are experimental alternatives, not changes to the proposed default method.

E1.justification: The training dataset and benchmark domains remain unchanged. Beyond v1's qualitative translation/pose perturbations, v2 adds systematic PROX-test coverage of corrupted metric initializations, including severe Gaussian depth shifts with standard deviation up to 5 m (Section S3).

E2.justification: The named external baselines remain unchanged. Table 3 adds two comparison variants against default GRAFT on both benchmarks: training with an additional V2S loss and with contact plus penetration losses.

E3.justification: The reported main training budget changes from 150k to 215k iterations, with cosine decay extended from 148k to 213k iterations after warmup. Section S3 adds a Gaussian depth-shift sweep evaluated using MPJPE and contact F1. Existing benchmark preprocessing and refinement counts remain unchanged; the newly stated 120k-step ablation budget is a disclosure, not an established budget change.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially: Table 3 tests whether explicit interaction losses help on both benchmarks, Section S3 quantifies sensitivity to initialization noise, and Section S8 reports that assigning one token per probe did not improve accuracy. These additions examine loss necessity, robustness, and token grouping beyond v1's existing component ablations and qualitative perturbations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Gaussian standard deviations specify input corruption, not statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces GRAFT's RICH-100 PA-MPJPE/F1 values of 49.30/0.565 with 46.32/0.578 and PROX-test values of 54.83/0.572 with 49.73/0.594. These accompany a changed training budget, not identical training conditions. Table 3 revises PROX ablation values and adds loss results; Section S3 adds robustness curves. Table 1 changes runtime from 0.38 to 0.2 seconds. External-baseline scores and user-study outcomes are retained.

T1.justification: The scale-update derivation and assumptions in Equations S1–S5, and the V2S/D2S definitions in Equations S6–S7, are unchanged. The added scale rationale and diagram explain existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the maximum interaction-improvement claim from 113% to 122%, and the abstract, introduction, and conclusion change the speed advantage from approximately 50× to 100×. The central contributions and dual-mode applicability claims remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 attributes benchmark-dependent behavior partly to training-domain similarity, interprets mixed loss-ablation results as supporting implicit contact learning, and argues that geometric refinement explains initialization robustness. The conclusion adds a limitation concerning Gaussian-perturbed training states and complex multi-contact interactions.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents surface-normal computation from four pointmap neighbors, the 120k-step ablation budget, and the user-study allocation of 15 internet images within each 20-image session. It also updates the main training schedule. These disclosures do not establish corresponding changes to previously undocumented implementation choices.

R1.justification: Related-work citations expand to include works such as BEDLAM2.0, CARI4D, and NSF. New Section S9 positions GRAFT alongside human generation and reconstruction research as complementary corrective refinement. The primary novelty positioning remains unchanged; publication-metadata updates are not new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds focused explanations of scale prediction and token grouping, edits the conclusion and captions, and inserts robustness and broader-context appendix sections. Most existing prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel robustness plot in Figure S3 and an explanatory scale-update diagram in Figure S5. Table 3 gains loss-variant rows, Table 2 adds RICH percentage annotations, and captions and figure placement are adjusted. Existing qualitative panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The new loss ablations and initialization-noise curves provide useful empirical support for existing design choices, while implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. These yield a modest net improvement. However, the strengthened 0.2-second/100× runtime claim is not reconciled with the retained Figure 6, which shows roughly 0.37 seconds at the stated three-step setting. The longer training budget also limits direct interpretation of the revised benchmark scores.
